name: Dogosé
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

sources.citation: Tauxier, Louis. 1931. Vocabulaires Dorhosié et Dorhosié-Finng. Journal de la Société des Africanistes 1(1): 87-110.
sources.note: 612-item Dorhosié wordlist collected Jan. 1922 at Nonokama, Nambota, Gangasé, Sousué, Sangobien, in French practical spelling with no accent or tone marks and no prosodic remark of any kind (grep for accent/ton/syllabe/prononc: 0 hits).

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid dogo1295 and reference tables for dogo1295 (35 refs), khis1238 (12), dogo1294 (9)
sources.note: Bibliography only: besides the items above it lists ~25 SIL literacy booklets in Dogosé (2000-2004), Armstrong wordlists, Tauxier 1931, Labouret 1958. No JIPA illustration, dissertation, or phonology article on Dogosé appears anywhere.

sources.citation: Tauxier, Louis. 1931. Les Dorhosié et Dorhosié-Finng du cercle de Bobo-Dioulasso (Soudan français). Journal de la Société des Africanistes 1(1): 61-86.
sources.note: Ethnographic notes on the Dorhosié (= Dogosé) and Dorhosié-Finng (= Dogoso); discusses classification (Delafosse's Bobo vs Lobi grouping) but nothing on pronunciation, accent or tone; the only 'accent' hit is 'une petite cicatrice, semblable à un accent aigu' (p. 63, a scarification simile). Text harvested page by page from Persée's page endpoints (PDF is behind an altcha challenge).

sources.citation: Winkelmann, Kerstin. 2007. B2. Dogose. In G. Miehe & K. Winkelmann (eds.), Noun class systems in Gur languages I: Southwestern Gur languages (without Gurunsi). Gur Monographs 9. Köln: Rüdiger Köppe.
